You are replacing the data source behind ONE adapter in a Python repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES:
  1. server/pipeline/contact_sources/linkedin_source.py   (edit it)
  2. fix-summary.md                                       (create it)

Touching any other file fails the check. Do NOT edit server/pipeline/contact_state.py, the other adapters, or the feeder.

## Why this is being changed

The podcast loop asks four channels 'have we already talked to this person' before it lets a cold first-contact email go out. If any first-order channel cannot be read, the verdict is UNKNOWN and nobody is cleared — deliberately, because a reconcile that reaches three of four sources and announces 'no prior contact' has laundered absence of evidence into evidence of absence.

This adapter reads a JSONL file at /mnt/d_drive/repos/open-engine/departments/sales/state/handoff/podcast_guest_linkedin.jsonl. That file has never existed. The process that would write it fail-closes on an AWS IAM grant that its own launcher documents as not yet made. So LinkedIn has reported unreachable on every run, and that single unwritable file holds the entire outreach loop shut.

Owner decision, 2026-08-11: read LinkedIn through Unipile, the same way the owner's own LinkedIn tooling does.

## What stays exactly as it is

`observe(people, *, client=None, now=None)` and `map_records(records, people)` are verified and must keep their behaviour and their signatures. `fetch(people)` must keep returning a list of NORMALISED records in the shape map_records already consumes:

    {"name": "Ada Lovelace", "sent_at": "2026-08-05T09:00:00+00:00",
     "direction": "outbound", "thread_ref": "li-thread-1"}

Only WHERE those records come from changes. An existing contract check drives this adapter with exactly that record shape and must keep passing.

## What to build

Replace `_JsonlLinkedInClient` and `build_client()`:

    class _UnipileLinkedInClient:
        def __init__(self, dsn, token, account_id, *, request=None):
            ...
        def fetch(self, people) -> list[dict]:
            ...

`request` is the injected transport seam and is what makes this checkable without calling Unipile. It is a callable `request(method, path, params=None) -> dict`. When it is None, build a default that performs a real HTTPS request against Unipile with the standard library only (no new dependency): base URL `https://<dsn>/api/v1`, header `X-API-KEY: <token>`, and GET `/chats` with `account_id` and a `limit`. Paginate only if it is simple to do so; one page is acceptable.

A chat page comes back as `{"items": [ ... ]}` where each chat looks like:

    {"id": "chat-77", "timestamp": "2026-08-05T09:00:00.000Z", "unread_count": 1,
     "attendees": [{"display_name": "Ada Lovelace", "id": "li-ada"}],
     "last_message": {"text": "...", "is_sender": 1}}

Normalise each chat into one record per attendee who is not the account owner: `name` from `display_name` (fall back to the chat's `name`), `sent_at` from the chat `timestamp` as an ISO-8601 string that KEEPS its UTC offset, `thread_ref` from the chat `id`, and `direction` "outbound" when `last_message.is_sender` is truthy else "inbound" (use "unknown" if you cannot tell; nothing downstream ranks on direction).

`build_client()` returns None — never raises — when credentials are absent, and accepts them in EITHER form:

  * three variables: UNIPILE_DSN, UNIPILE_ACCESS_TOKEN, UNIPILE_LINKEDIN_ACCOUNT_ID
  * one variable LINKEDIN_UNIPILE_CREDENTIALS holding a JSON object with those three keys, which is how a single secret reference arrives

It must NOT make a network call while merely being constructed; it runs on every feeder invocation, including ones where LinkedIn will never be consulted.

## Three rules the check enforces, and why

1. NO MESSAGE TEXT ANYWHERE. `last_message.text` is a real conversation from the owner's real inbox. It must not appear in a record, an observation, an evidence_ref or a coverage detail. Carry who, when, which channel, and the chat id.

2. NO CREDENTIAL ANYWHERE. The DSN, token and account id must never appear in a record, an observation, or a coverage detail — coverage details are written verbatim into receipts. When you build the failure detail from an exception, make sure the exception text cannot carry the URL or the token; scrub them.

3. A FAILED READ IS NOT AN EMPTY INBOX. If the transport raises, `observe` reports `reached=False` with a one-line reason and zero observations. If the read succeeds and simply finds nobody, it reports `reached=True` with zero observations, because a genuinely untouched prospect must still be clearable. Timestamps must be timezone-aware; the resolver ranks a LinkedIn touch against Gmail and Bee purely by time.

## Run BOTH checks until each prints PASS

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/contact_source_check.py --worktree "$PWD" --source linkedin --owned server/pipeline/contact_sources/linkedin_source.py
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u16_linkedin_unipile_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

The first is the unchanged contract; the second is the new source. Read the failure text, it names what is expected.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of BOTH check commands. Under 400 words.

You are changing ONE invocation in ONE bash script. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES:
  1. scripts/run_podcast_loop.sh   (edit it)
  2. fix-summary.md                (create it)

Touching any other file fails the check. Do not touch any Python file.

## The problem

In the `guest-acquisition` branch of that script there is a call to scripts/guest_candidate_feed.py, roughly:

    if ! "$PYTHON_BIN" "$REPO/scripts/guest_candidate_feed.py" \
          --inbox "$GUEST_CANDIDATE_INBOX" \
          --ledger "$GUEST_FUNNEL_LEDGER" \
          --out "$GUEST_CANDIDATES" >> "$LOG" 2>&1; then

Until yesterday that script only read two JSON files, so it needed nothing. It now decides who is safe to cold-email by reading four contact channels — Gmail, LinkedIn, Bee and HubSpot — and it is invoked with none of the credentials any of them need. A channel it cannot authenticate to must be reported as unread, and an unread first-order channel holds every candidate.

So this does not fail loudly. It produces a permanent, polite, fully-receipted zero that looks exactly like a week with no good guests in it.

A few lines further down, the PRODUCER step in the same branch is already wrapped correctly. Read it: it uses scripts/secret_exec.py with --secret-env to inject a HubSpot key, then `env` to pass the Gmail token path, and only then runs the Python module. Copy that pattern.

## What to change

Wrap the feeder invocation the same way, so the feeder process receives:

  * the Gmail token path, as the producer step passes it — both GMAIL_CREDENTIALS_PATH and GMAIL_FULL_TOKEN_PATH set to "$GMAIL_FULL_TOKEN", which the script already computes near the top;
  * the HubSpot key, via --secret-env HUBSPOT_API_KEY=mybcat/integrations/api-keys/hubspot, exactly as the producer step does;
  * the LinkedIn Unipile credentials, from the secret mybcat/integrations/oauth/linkedin-unipile. That secret holds a JSON object with the keys UNIPILE_DSN, UNIPILE_ACCESS_TOKEN and UNIPILE_LINKEDIN_ACCOUNT_ID. secret_exec.py accepts --secret-env repeatedly and supports selecting one JSON field with ENV=SECRET_ID:FIELD, so you can inject the three separately; verified working. Alternatively inject the whole object as LINKEDIN_UNIPILE_CREDENTIALS. Either is accepted.

Everything else about the invocation stays: the same three arguments, the same append to "$LOG", the same `if ! ... ; then` failure branch with its telegram message and its obe_loop_verdict call, the same exit 1. The failure branch is load-bearing — the feeder failing must still refuse the run rather than let the producer see an empty pool it cannot tell from a real drought.

HARD RULES:
  * No credential value may appear in the file. Only secret references and $VARIABLES. Nothing else.
  * Do not print, echo or log any of these variables.
  * Do not change the producer step, the ceiling-count step, or any other loop branch.

## Run the exact check until it prints PASS

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u17_feeder_env_arrival_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

This one does not grep. It extracts your invocation from the script and EXECUTES it against a stand-in interpreter that records which variables actually arrived at the feeder process — names only, never values — and against a stand-in for secret_exec so nothing reaches AWS. It also runs `bash -n` over the whole script, so a syntax error anywhere fails it.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of the check command. Under 'Risk' say what happens on the next scheduled run if one of these secret references is wrong or unreadable. Under 400 words.

The inherited environment is scrubbed of those variables first, so a variable exported in the operator's shell cannot be mistaken for wiring that the script performs. It also parses the whole script and rejects any literal credential.
